source.title: Fathers' versus mothers' social referencing signals in relation to infant anxiety and avoidance: a visual cliff experiment

confidence_rationale: Social referencing is the empirical situation where ARC-094's three terms are unavoidably present at once -- the infant (self) reads the parent's affect (other) in order to evaluate the drop (object) -- and this is a reasonably powered experimental instance of it (81 infants, randomised to parent). Supports the claim that the object is the medium through which another's affect becomes usable rather than a bystander. Held at 0.62 because the study was designed to test a parent-gender question, not the architecture: the triadic structure is the paradigm's premise, so the paper assumes it rather than testing it.
failure_signatures: The triadic self-object-other structure is the visual cliff paradigm's PREMISE, not its finding, so this entry cannot be cited as evidence that the structure exists -- only that it is the established way to operationalise infant affect-reading, and that it behaves lawfully.

Parental encouragement alone had no relationship to infant anxiety or avoidance, and only PATERNAL expressed anxiety predicted infant anxiety and avoidance -- so the affect transmitted across the triad is selective by signal valence and by which adult sends it, not a general other-to-self affect channel.

Infant temperament moderated the paternal effect, so the mapping from another's displayed affect to the infant's own state is gated by the receiver's prior disposition rather than being a fixed transfer.

mapping.source_claim_statement: 81 infants aged 10-15 months were randomised to a father (n=41) or mother (n=40) condition on a visual cliff, with the parent at the deep side encouraging the infant to cross. Mothers showed more intense facial encouragement but infants crossed equally fast with comparable anxiety. Paternal, but not maternal, expressed anxiety was positively associated with infant expressed anxiety and avoidance, moderated by infant temperament; parental encouragement alone was unrelated to either outcome.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the convergence point of the two senses of 'object' ARC-094 intends. The infant cannot evaluate the drop from its own resources, so it reads the parent's face -- and the parent's affect is only usable BECAUSE it is about the drop. Self, object and other are bound in a single act, with the object supplying the referent that makes the other's affective signal interpretable. That is the object stage doing work: not a way-station on a path from self to other, but the thing that gives the other's state content the self can act on.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The design tests a parent-gender hypothesis and takes the triadic structure for granted, so it illustrates the object stage rather than evidencing it -- a paradigm's premise cannot also be its result. The selective findings also complicate the simple reading: only paternal anxiety transmitted, encouragement did not transmit at all, and infant temperament gated the effect, so this is not a clean other-to-self affect channel. Finally, 10-15 months is well after the fast/cognitive split ARC-094 cares about is presumed to begin, so it speaks to the stage's operation rather than to its ontogenetic ordering.
mapping.source_context: Human infants 10-15 months; randomised visual cliff experiment; Dutch community sample.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality reflects an adequately powered randomised developmental experiment in a good journal. mapping_fidelity is the limiting term: the paper illustrates the triad rather than testing it, and its actual findings are about parent gender, which is orthogonal to ARC-094.
